prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2, plain light background, crisp vanilla Minecraft voxel blocks and textures only, no characters or animals. Two views side by side at the same block scale: LEFT straight-on NORTH front elevation, orthographic; RIGHT elevated NORTHWEST three-quarter view showing the depth of the whole 34 x 34 lot. Small headings FRONT and THREE-QUARTER only. Skilled human builder quality: convincing massing, proud walls, recessed framed openings, slab and stair detail, deep eaves, roof verges and ridge, fences, trapdoors and lanterns. Do not smooth blocks into real-world objects.
Site: 1950s California mid-century modern house, flat suburban desert lot, hard desert sunlight. Main body 22 blocks wide, long low single storey, white_concrete stucco on thin smooth_stone_slab base. Total site 34 wide along street x 34 deep, maximum 8 tall, ridge about 7, chimney 8. Very low gable roof made of pale grey smooth_stone_slab, ridge parallel to street rising only 1.5 blocks; thin dark_oak_slab fascia, 2-block deep eaves. dark_oak_log beam ends project past front and back eaves every 3 blocks above continuous dark_oak_planks header. Almost blank north street facade: left freestanding tan mud_bricks/packed_mud/mud_brick_slab ledgestone wall one block proud, next recessed bold acacia_door between orange_concrete panels; right thin glass_pane clerestory under eave split by dark timber mullions. Both gable ends have thin clerestories.
At west (left) end, flat carport roof one level below main eave on slender dark_oak_fence posts, rear pierced white_concrete breeze-block screen built with actual square gaps. Pale smooth_stone driveway with light_gray_concrete joint lines, long low block-built 1950s car: cyan_concrete teal body, white_concrete roof, iron_block and iron_trapdoor chrome bumpers, black_concrete tyres. Low block-built mailbox at head of driveway. Front sand yard with gravel beds, tall cactus cluster, two jungle_log/jungle_leaves palms, three smooth_stone_slab stepping pads from sidewalk to door, sparse dead_bush and short_grass.
Central open-air glass_pane-ringed atrium courtyard crossed by one exposed dark_oak_log beam; retain an actual roof opening. South garden facade floor-to-ceiling glass_pane between thin dark posts, sliding glass openings onto smooth_stone patio. Behind house turquoise water pool lined light_blue_concrete, stepped voxel kidney outline with smooth_quartz_slab white coping, concrete deck and grass_block lawn, third palm in rear corner. Right elevated view should reveal the courtyard opening and some rear pool beyond the house without removing walls or roofs.
Exact allowed block palette by role (use these ids as construction guidance, not an enormous printed legend):
stucco: white_concrete; structure: dark_oak_log; header: dark_oak_planks; fascia: dark_oak_slab; base_paving: smooth_stone, smooth_stone_slab; roof_deck: smooth_stone_slab; driveway_joints: light_gray_concrete; ledgestone: mud_bricks, packed_mud, mud_brick_slab; glass: glass_pane; front_door: acacia_door; utility_door: dark_oak_door; accent: orange_concrete; pool: water, light_blue_concrete, smooth_quartz_slab; pit_floor: smooth_quartz, smooth_quartz_stairs; ground: sand, gravel, grass_block, dirt; floor_public: smooth_stone, light_gray_concrete, white_concrete; floor_bedrooms: spruce_planks; floor_baths: smooth_quartz; ceiling: spruce_planks; wall_panelling: spruce_trapdoor, spruce_stairs, spruce_slab, spruce_planks, spruce_fence; partitions: white_concrete; fireplace/chimney: mud_bricks, black_concrete, campfire, smooth_stone_slab.
Allowed functional/decor blocks: cyan_concrete, yellow_concrete, red_concrete, iron_block, black_concrete, cactus, jungle_log, jungle_leaves, large_fern, potted_cactus, dead_bush, short_grass, lantern, sea_lantern, end_rod, daylight_detector, dark_oak_fence, orange_carpet, white_carpet, cyan_carpet, yellow_carpet, smooth_red_sandstone_stairs, quartz_stairs, quartz_slab, smooth_quartz_stairs, birch_planks, birch_slab, birch_stairs, birch_trapdoor, iron_trapdoor, spruce_fence, spruce_slab, spruce_stairs, spruce_trapdoor, lectern, bookshelf, flower_pot, item_frame, barrel, smoker, furnace, cauldron, orange_bed, cyan_bed, yellow_bed, light_blue_bed, white_bed. Only show furnishings if actually visible. Add small readable exact-id callouts to main materials: white_concrete, smooth_stone_slab, dark_oak_slab, dark_oak_log, mud_bricks, acacia_door, glass_pane, cyan_concrete, cactus. No invented block shapes, round tyres, curved pool edges, photorealism, extra storeys, people or animals.
changes: Saved the unmodified generated image as concept.png in the current directory.
Block ids are visual interpretations, not recoverable block data. The roles retain all planned blocks; concealed interior materials and furnishings cannot be confirmed from this exterior image.
A bottom row of nine material-detail thumbnails was added to the two requested views.
The two views use different apparent scales, and the right view is substantially elevated.
The roof appears as broad stepped courses with masonry-like textures rather than faithful smooth_stone_slab textures; its exact rise and two-block eave depth cannot be verified.
The carport roof merges into the main roof instead of clearly sitting one level lower; its supports appear closer to full logs than slender fences.
The ledgestone wall reads as a facade panel rather than a clearly freestanding wall one block proud.
The tan masonry texture and brown front door do not accurately match vanilla mud_bricks and acacia_door appearances.
The breeze-block screen uses small inset holes that cannot be reproduced at the depicted scale with white_concrete alone.
The beam-end spacing, 22-block house width, 34-by-34 lot dimensions and eight-block height are not reliably countable.
The pool is a stepped rounded rectangle rather than a kidney shape; white stair-like corner coping and poolside seating were added.
The atrium opening and crossing beam are visible, but the south sliding doors, full garden glass wall and gable-end clerestories are not clearly shown.
The front elevation appears to contain more than three stepping pads; the perspective view more closely follows the requested three.
The palms have dense broadleaf crowns rather than palm-shaped fronds, and additional shrubs fill the planting beds.
A gray street, low rear boundary wall, entry lantern and masonry mailbox were added.
The car is relatively short and boxy; its headlights, chrome trim and wheel hubs contain details that do not map cleanly to vanilla block geometry.
No interior beds, appliances, fireplace fire or sunken pit are visible.
